title: Project: a web application
goal: Build a small application around one complete user task.
explanation: A task tracker can teach create, read, update and delete operations. Start with local in-memory state before adding persistence or a backend.
Design empty, loading, success and failure states. Preserve useful input when an operation fails. Treat browser storage as local convenience, not secure server storage.
If you add accounts, authorisation belongs on the server for each record. Do not treat a user id from a browser request as proof of identity.
exercise: Build a task list with add, complete and delete. Write down how a failed save should behave.
hint: Keep one complete flow working before adding accounts or multiple screens.

quiz.question: What should happen to useful form input after a failed save?
options: Preserve it so the user can retry
quiz.explanation: Preserving input helps the person recover without repeating their work.
